summary: Coos County, OR: 50-foot wooden tower built in 1965 by the Coos Forest Protective Association near Sitkum; removed or dismantled in 1989 or the 1980s; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 50-foot wooden live-in tower with a 14-by-14-foot cabin (CT3 per Forest Lookouts)
facts.status_note: Tower removed around 1989 (register and firelookout.com) or in the 1980s (a Dora event report in The World); no source describes what remains
facts.agency: Coos Forest Protective Association (listed as Coos FPA)

events.note: 50-foot tower with a 14 x 14 cabin; register and firelookout.com give 1965, Forest Lookouts quotes a 1965 Coos District annual report
Lookouts in the Elk Mountain tower began scanning for smoke over Dora, Sitkum and the surrounding area
Register says removed in 1989; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1989; The World's Dora event report says dismantled in the 1980s
Registered December 10, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: built 1965 as a 50-foot wooden live-in tower; removed 1989
evidence.quote: Built in 1965, this 50' wooden live-in tower was removed in 1989.

evidence.supports: about three miles southwest of Sitkum
evidence.quote: a 50-foot structure erected on Elk Mountain about three miles southwest of Sitkum
A new 50 foot CT3 tower with a 14 x 14 cabin was constructed on Elk Mountain

evidence.supports: $4,000 credit from State Restoration Fund tied to loss of Brushy Bald Lookout
evidence.quote: using a $4,000 credit from State Restoration Fund for the loss of Brushy Bald Lookout

evidence.supports: second CFPA tower ready on Elk Mountain in 1965
evidence.quote: CFPA had a second tower ready to use in 1965, this time on Elk Mountain.

evidence.supports: earlier tower near Brewster Rock decommissioned after summer 1964
evidence.quote: After the summer of 1964, that tower was decommissioned.
Beginning in 1965, lookouts in the tower on Elk Mountain scanned for smoke in Dora, Sitkum, and the surrounding area.

evidence.supports: watched forests around the East Fork of the Coquille River
evidence.quote: First from a tower located near Brewster Rock and later from a tower on Elk Mountain, lookouts watched for fires in the forests surrounding the East Fork of the Coquille River.
The Elk Mountain tower was dismantled in the 1980s.

evidence.supports: source of the 1965 tower report: Coos District Annual Report
CFPA expanded as Coos Forest Protective Association

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says removed in 1989 and firelookout.com says destroyed in 1989. The World's Dora event report says dismantled in the 1980s, which fits the same period. The sources differ on how the tower ended, not on roughly when.

sources.title: Champion trees and lookout towers discussed at Dora event

notes_for_editor: Build year 1965 is consistent across four sources. Removal wording differs (removed, destroyed, dismantled); years agree at 1989 or the 1980s. The brief's coordinates match the register (N 43.133360, W 123.925130). The Dora event report names lookouts only at Brewster Rock, not this site, so no staff names were used. The earlier Brewster Rock tower is not this record. Current site condition and access are not described in any source read. Do not confuse with Elk Mountain (Hood River County, US 592) or the Elk Mountain in Wallowa County (US 1614).
